title: Particle Post
intro: Put up with, put off, put down — same verb, three different meanings.

A2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘stop the TV or lights’?
A2.why: “Off” stops things: “turn off” the TV. “Turn down” only makes it quieter or lower.

A2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘increase the volume’?
A2.why: “Up” means more: “turn up” the volume. “Turn on” only starts it.

A2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘start a machine’?
A2.why: “On” starts things: “turn on” the radio. “Off” stops them.
“Go on” means continue: “Go on, I'm listening.”

A2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘enter a room’?
A2.why: “In” means inside: “go in” is “entrar”. “Go on” means continue.

A2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘remove your clothes’?
A2.why: “Off” means away from the body: “take off” your coat or your hat.

A2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘start a new hobby’?
A2.why: To “take up” a hobby is to start it: “I took up painting.”

A2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘wake up and leave bed’?
A2.why: “Get up” means leave your bed. “Wake up” is just opening your eyes.

A2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘leave a bus or train’?
A2.why: Buses, trains and planes: “get on” to board, “get off” to leave.

A2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘search for something you have lost’?
A2.why: “Look for” means search, “buscar”. “Look at” is just “mirar”.

A2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘take a seat’?
A2.why: “Sit down” means take a seat. “Sit up” means straighten your back.

A2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘return to a place’?

B1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘tolerate something unpleasant’?
B1.why: “Put up with” means “aguantar”: “I can't put up with the noise.”
“Put off” means postpone, “aplazar”: “We put off the trip until May.”

B1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘write something on paper’?
B1.why: “Put down” on paper means write it: “Put your name down here.”
“Give up” means stop trying, or quit: “He gave up smoking.”

B1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘finally agree after resisting’?
B1.why: “Give in” means stop resisting, “ceder”. “Give up” means abandon.

B1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘donate something for free’?
Which phrasal verb means ‘recover from an illness or shock’?
B1.why: To “get over” an illness or a shock is to recover from it: “superarlo”.

B1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘leave a bus or train’?
B1.why: Leave a bus or train: “get off”. Board it: “get on”.

B1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘rise from bed’?
Which phrasal verb means ‘take care of someone’?
B1.why: “Look after” means “cuidar”: “She looks after her grandchildren.”

B1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘check a word in a dictionary’?
B1.why: “Look up” a word: search for it in a dictionary or online.

B1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘have a friendly relationship with someone’?
B1.why: “Get on with” someone means you get along well: “llevarse bien”.

B2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘solve a problem, or exercise’?
B2.why: “Work out” means solve a problem, and also do exercise at the gym.

B2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘try to improve something’?
B2.why: To “work on” something is to put effort into improving it.

B2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘gradually develop an appetite or a sweat’?
B2.why: “Work up an appetite” or “a sweat”: build it up little by little.

B2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘stop functioning, or become upset’?
B2.why: “Break down”: a car stops working, or a person starts crying.

B2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘end a relationship’?
B2.why: “Break up” means end a relationship: “romper con alguien”.

B2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘escape, or suddenly start (a fire, a war)’?
B2.why: “Break out”: prisoners escape, or a fire or war suddenly starts.

B2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘perform or execute a plan’?
B2.why: “Carry out” a plan, a task or an operation: “llevar a cabo”.

B2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘become overexcited’ (usually ‘get carried away’)?
B2.why: “Get carried away”: lose control because you're too excited.
“Look into” means investigate: “The sheriff looked into the robbery.”

B2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘reduce the amount of something you eat or use’?
B2.why: “Cut down on” means reduce: “The doctor told me to cut down on salt.”

B2.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘stop the supply of water, gas or electricity’?
B2.why: “Cut off” means stop a supply: “The town's water was cut off.”

C1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘invent an idea’?
C1.why: “Come up with” an idea, a plan or a solution: think of it.

C1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘find something by chance’?
C1.why: “Come across” means find or meet by chance: “toparse con”.

C1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘become ill with’?
C1.why: “Come down with” a cold or the flu: start to be ill.

C1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘reject an offer’?
C1.why: To “turn down” an offer is to refuse it: “rechazar”.

C1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘result in a particular way’?
C1.why: “Turn out” means end up or prove to be: “resultar”.

C1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘arrive, often unexpectedly’?
C1.why: “Turn up” means arrive or appear, often without warning.

C1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘defend or support someone’?
C1.why: To “stand up for” someone is to defend them.

C1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘be ready to help if needed’?
C1.why: “Stand by” means be ready to help, or stay loyal to someone.

C1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘be noticeably different or better’?
C1.why: “Stand out” means be easy to notice: “destacar”.

C1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘invent a false story or excuse’?
C1.why: To “make up” a story or an excuse is to invent it.

C1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘see or hear something with difficulty’?
C1.why: “Make out” means see or hear with difficulty: “distinguir”.

C1.q: Which phrasal verb means ‘move towards a place’?
C1.why: To “make for” a place is to head towards it: “The riders made for the hills.”
